blogs.title: Instant Pot Pulled Pork
blogs.subtitle: Tender, smoky, and ready in under an hour
instructions: Season the pork shoulder generously with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Place all ingredients in the Instant Pot and stir to combine.
Set to high pressure and cook for 45 minutes.
Allow pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick release.
Shred the pork with two forks and toss with the remaining sauce.
Serve on buns or over rice.
blogs.content: This Instant Pot pulled pork is perfect for a quick and easy meal without sacrificing flavor. In just under an hour you get tender, juicy pork ready to serve.

blogs.title: Best Grilled Salmon
blogs.subtitle: Healthy, flaky, and on the table in 20 minutes
instructions: Brush the salmon fillets with olive oil and lemon juice.
Sprinkle with garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes per side, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Serve with a side of vegetables or a fresh salad.
blogs.content: Our grilled salmon combines healthiness with great taste. Perfectly grilled to bring out the rich flavors of the fish, it is sure to impress your guests.

blogs.title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
blogs.subtitle: Light, airy stacks for a lazy weekend
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda.
In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, and melted butter.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry until just combined; lumps are fine.
Cook 1/4-cup portions on a buttered griddle over medium heat until bubbles form, then flip.
Serve warm with maple syrup.
blogs.content: The buttermilk and a touch of baking soda are the secret to tall, tender pancakes every time.

blogs.title: Classic Margherita Pizza
blogs.subtitle: Blistered crust, basil, and fresh mozzarella
instructions: Preheat your oven (with a stone or steel) to its highest setting, ideally 500F+.
Stretch the dough into a 10-inch round on a floured peel.
Spread the crushed tomatoes, season with salt, and tear the mozzarella over the top.
Bake 8-12 minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese bubbles.
Finish with fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
blogs.content: A handful of quality ingredients and a screaming-hot oven are all you need for pizzeria-style results at home.

blogs.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
blogs.subtitle: Gooey centers in individual ramekins
instructions: Butter and lightly flour four ramekins; preheat the oven to 425F.
Melt the chocolate and butter together until smooth.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, and sugar until pale, then fold in the chocolate and flour.
Divide among the ramekins and bake 12-14 minutes until the edges are set but the centers jiggle.
Invert onto plates and serve immediately.
blogs.content: The trick is to pull them while the centers are still soft — a minute too long and you lose the molten flow.

blogs.title: Thai Green Curry with Vegetables
blogs.subtitle: Fragrant, creamy, and weeknight-fast

ingredients.name: Thai basil and lime to finish

instructions: Fry the curry paste in a splash of coconut milk until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the vegetables and simmer 8-10 minutes until crisp-tender.
Season with soy sauce; finish with Thai basil and a squeeze of lime.
Serve over jasmine rice.
blogs.content: Blooming the curry paste in fat first is what unlocks its full aroma — don't skip it.
